This is a revision against summoning order dated 10.06.2025 passed by the then Ld. ACJM,
South whereby the revisionists herein were summoned for the offence punishable u/s 323/352/341/356/379 IPC.
2.0

The brief facts relevant for adjudication of the present revision are that a complaint u/s 156(3)
Cr.PC was filed by the respondent herein with the allegations that on 08.10.2018, at about 3PM, at T point, Khirki Village, near Saket Courts complex, //1// when he stopped his auto for his passengers to get down, one traffic police official caught hold of his collar, threw him on the road, beat him up,
tore his uniform, and demanded illegal gratification of Rs.2000/- from him.
When the respondent opposed, the traffic constable forcibly took out Rs.1850/- from him, slapped him multiple times, and impounded his autorickshaw.

Thereafter, PCR reached the spot and the PCR officials took him to the police station instead of the hospital, where, HC Karambir refused to take the respondent to the hospital but instead abused him.

HC Attar Singh, of the PCR van informed the respondent that since Hc Karambir Singh And Anr vs The State Govt Of Nct Delhi And Anr on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59199130/
1 he has not suffered any grievous injuries, he would not be taken for any medical examination.
However, on account of repeated insistence for several hours, HC Karambir Singh took the respondent for his medical examination to Jai Prakash Narayan Trauma Centre, but at some distance from the hospital, HC Karambir made the respondent get down from the bike, slapped him,
and forced him to sign several blank papers.

sentences.text: Even inside the hospital, appellant no.1 HC Karambir misspoke about the respondent to the doctors, and finally left him stranded over there.

Ld. ACJM (South) took cognizance of the offence as disclosed in the complaint and the respondent no.2 /
complainant was given opportunity to lead pre- summoning evidence.

Respondent no.2 /
complainant examined five witnesses in support of his case, including himself.
After hearing the submissions of both the parties, the Ld. Trial Court vide order dated 10.06.2025, summoned the revisionists herein.
Aggrieved by the said order, the revisionists herein have preferred this criminal revision.

3.0 It is argued on behalf of the revisionist that the incident took place on 08.10.2018, and the respondent no. 2 made a //2// PCR call at about 15:39hrs alleging seizure of his auto by police officials, thereafter, he made another call at 16:16hrs about physical injury and again at 18:33 hrs regarding requirement of police assistance and being injured.
However, he did not mention the name of any the police officers in any DD or 100 number call or at hospital.
The PCR calls were inconsistent and self contradictory in nature.
Even the MLC records that the respondent no. 2 suffers no physical injury.
It is further argued that the respondent No. 2 concocted a false story as his autorickshaw was seized by the police u/s 66 of Delhi Police Act.
It is further argued that the respondent no. 2 did not produce any cogent evidence regarding his allegation of extortion, assault or threat by the revisionists.
It is submitted that the actions taken by the revisionist were in their official course of duties, for which sanction u/s 197 Cr.PC is required.

Further, that even in the application for release of vehicle, the respondent no. 2 did not allege of any beatings by the police officials and mentioned that the vehicle was found in abandoned condition.
It is further submitted that nothing incriminating was found even in the vigilance enquiry conducted by the ACP concerned.

In support, Ld. Counsel for revisionist relied upon Sita Ram Mishra Vs. Praveen Kumar,
Crl. MC No. 6874/2025 dated 24.09.2025, DT Virupakshappa Vs. C. Subhash, Crl Appeal No.
722/2015 decided on 27.04.2015 and Anil Kumar & ors. Vs. MK Aiyappa & Anr., Crl Appeal No.
1590-91 of 2013 decided on 01.10.2013 3.1 Ld.

Counsel for the respondent no. 2 submits that the Ld.
Trial Court has passed a reasoned order.

It is submitted that the revisionists have taken the plea that sanction u/s 197 Cr.PC is required for their prosecution, however, the offences committed by //3//
the petitioners are not falling in the colour of the duty or in the discharge of the official duty.
It is also submitted that an independent witness was examined the respondent no. 2 before the Ld. Trial Court, therefore, the plea of the revisionist that there is no independent witness is false.
4.0 I have heard the arguments advanced by both the sides and perused the record carefully.
5.0 The allegations as levelled by the revisionist in the complaint are serious in nature.
The fact whether the respondents had nothing to do with the offence would come to light only after trial is conducted in the matter.

Further the incident is stated to be outside the Saket Court complex which is surrounded by numerous CCTV cameras but the police inadvertently or knowingly did not opt to obtain the CCTV footage from the same.

Further, with regard to the factum of sanction u/s Hc Karambir Singh And Anr vs The State Govt Of Nct Delhi And Anr on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59199130/
2 197Cr.PC, the same cannot be afforded to the revisionists as their acts had no nexus with their official duty.

In Om Kr. Dhankar vs State Of Haryana & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 464 of 2012 decided on 28.02.2012, the point of requirement of sanction u/s 197 Cr.PC was discussed and it was observed as under:
"11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The second question, is whether sanction under Section 197 Cr.P.C. is mandatorily required for the prosecution of respondent No. 2 for the offences under Sections 420, 406 and 161 IPC as he happened to be Deputy Excise and Taxation Commissioner at the time of incident.
In our view, the controversy with regard to the second question is concluded by the decision of this Court in Prakash Singh Badal and Another Vs. State of Punjab and Others7.

entities.text: Prakash Singh Badal and Another Vs. State of Punjab and Others7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra case (supra) was 6 (2006) 1 SCC 557 7 (2007) 1 SCC 1 considered in Prakash Singh Badal case (supra) in para 49 of the report.

This Court thus held that the //4// offence of cheating under Section 420 or for that matter offences relateable to Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B can by no stretch of imagination by their very nature be regarded as having been committed by any public servant while acting or purporting to act in discharge of official duty.

This Court stated in paragraphs 49 and 50 of the report thus:
"49. Great emphasis has been laid on certain decisions of this Court to show that even in relation to the offences punishable under Sections 467 and 468 sanction is necessary.
The foundation of the position has reference to some offences in Rakesh Kumar Mishra case.

That decision has no relevance because ultimately this Court has held that the absence of search warrant was intricately (sic linked) with the making of search and the allegations about alleged offences had their matrix on the absence of search warrant and other circumstances had a determinative role in the issue.
A decision is an authority for what it actually decides.
Reference to a particular sentence in the context of the factual scenario cannot be read out of context.

50. The offence of cheating under Section 420 or for that matter offences relatable to Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B can by no stretch of imagination by their very nature be regarded as having been committed by any public servant while acting or purporting to act in discharge of official duty.
In such cases, official status only provides an opportunity for commission of the offence."

6.0 In view of the above legal position, Ld. ACJM has rightly observed that for prosecuting the respondent No. 2 for the offences for which the summoning order has been issued, the sanction of the competent authority under Section 197 Cr.P.C. is not required.
The Ld. ACJM has considered all the relevant factors and has come to a reasoned finding.
Thus, in view of the detailed order passed by the Ld. Trial Court, I do not find any infirmity and irregularity in the same.
The same does not warrant any interference.
